description: A list of AI autonomous agents

summary.one_liner: A curated, community-maintained Markdown list of AI agent products, split into open-source projects and closed-source projects and companies, with categories and short descriptions for each entry.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" link list rather than a software project. The README sorts entries into two sections: open-source projects and closed-source projects and companies. Each entry gets a short description, a category tag (such as General purpose, Coding, Multi-agent, Build-your-own, Data analysis, or Productivity), and links to its GitHub repo, website, paper, or docs. The visible portion covers open-source agents such as AutoGPT, BabyAGI and its many "Baby" mods, AutoGen, CrewAI, AgentGPT, Aider, GPT Engineer, ChatDev, and Devika. The web version of the list can be filtered by category and use case. The README states the list is not comprehensive, and it asks contributors to add entries in alphabetical order within the correct category. The README is truncated, so the closed-source section and the end of the list were not visible.
use_cases: Finding an open-source AI agent for a specific task
Comparing autonomous agent frameworks like AutoGPT and BabyAGI
Discovering coding agents that write, debug, or migrate code
Looking up multi-agent frameworks for building LLM systems
Browsing AI agent products by category
Finding no-code or low-code agent builders
notable: Splits entries into open-source and closed-source sections
Tags each entry with categories and use cases, filterable in the companion web version
Covers many BabyAGI-derived mods with notes on their differences
Linked from E2B, which promotes its Code Interpreter SDK throughout the README
caveats: The README is not comprehensive, according to its own statement
The README is truncated, so the closed-source section and the rest of the list were not visible
Entries are self-described and not verified by the list itself
